newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Mayor orders Indonesia's Megawati to close office.
newsitem.headline: Mayor orders Indonesia's Megawati to close office.

text.p: Indonesian officials have ordered ousted minority party leader Megawati Sukarnoputri to close her party office two weeks after it was opened in defiance of the military, party officials said on Tuesday.

East Jakarta Mayor Sudarsono said in the notice of closure, a copy of which was obtained by Reuters, that he had taken the action after receiving letters from local residents that the use of the building was not in accordance with regulations.

"Megawati Sukarnoputri and (secretary-general) Alexander Litaay are ordered to soon stop activities of a secretariat of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) Megawati faction within 72 hours of the receipt of this letter," said the order, dated September 23.
Party officials said the letter was received about 7 p.m. on Monday.

"If you do not in the near future comply with this order, the government of Jakarta represented by Mayor of East Jakarta will implement the closure and all risks will be borne by you," the letter said.
Litaay told Reuters: "We are still discussing our next step."
The military has said Megawati and her followers do not have the right to carry out political activities and that the opening of a headquarters was unacceptable.

Megawati's supporters opened the office on September 9 after they were evicted from the PDI central headquarters by police on July 27. They had taken over that building in June when Megawati, the daughter of late founding president Sukarno, was ousted from the PDI leadership by a government-backed faction.
At least five people died and 149 people were injured in riots triggered by the police raid.

The government has said it only recognises the rival faction as the legitimate representative of the PDI. Megawati has challenged the decision and a lawsuit demanding that her ouster be declared illegal is pending before a Jakarta court.
